subject: Pilot: developer boarding playlist — SDK install, auth & reranker test
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@archtech.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot: developer boarding playlist — SDK install, auth & reranker test

Claire — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a compact "developer playlist" you can hand to your engineers to get a local proof-of-concept running this week. I attached the playbook and a small sample reranker app for a runnable test.

Top-line recap:
- Goal: 1-week dev pilot that validates routing, auth, structured output/tool-calling, and a simple embeddings + reranker proof.
- Success criteria: reproducible local run, end-to-end request demonstrating
  - Auth handshake with API key (dev)
  - Tokenized routing to a low-cost candidate model + reranker step
  - Structured JSON output with tool-call placeholder

Immediate asks for ArchTech engineers:
1) Follow the attached redwood-dev-playlist.md — it contains the SDK install steps for Python and TypeScript, plus a short local sandbox checklist.
2) Use auth-config-example.env to populate REDWOOD_API_KEY and OPTIONAL_LOCAL_ENDPOINT if you want to run the sample against a local stub.
3) Run the sample-reranker-app (tarball attached) and confirm we can reproduce the rerank output in the sample test file sample_input.json.

Next steps (owner):
- ArchTech: run the "local run" section and share logs (expected <5 minutes wall-clock) — Claire to coordinate engineering time.
- Redwood: Aditya will provide a compact routing example (Python + TS) and a suggested batching profile. Jordan will help with embedding dimensionality and reranker config.
- Schedule: propose a 30-min sync on Monday (04/08) to validate outputs and align on metrics.

Attachments included: redwood-dev-playlist.md, sample-reranker-app.tar.gz, auth-config-example.env, local-test-checklist.pdf

If anything in the playlist looks out of scope, call it out and we can pare down the first test to just embeddings -> rerank.

— Tessa

Subject: Re: Pilot: developer boarding playlist — SDK install, auth & reranker test

Tessa — thanks for the clear playbook. Rahul and I reviewed the attachment and we have a couple quick clarifying questions before our engineers dig in: 

1) For the reranker tarball, does the sample include a small on-disk index or does it call out to an embedding service? If it's the latter, we want the offline index option for the local run.
2) Are there recommended model sizes for the candidate/rescoring split so we can size our dev VMs (we have a mix of 8GB and 16GB GPUs)?
3) Does the auth-config-example.env include a short TTL token flow we can wire into our internal test harness, or should we implement the simple static API_KEY approach for the first pass?

We aim to run the local test on Friday (04/06) morning. If the local index is available that helps speed things up.

— Claire
Claire Ng
Head of Integrations, ArchTech Systems
claire@archtech.io

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@archtech.io>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-05T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: developer boarding playlist — SDK install, auth & reranker test

Claire — quick answers inline and a minimal code snippet reference.

1) Reranker packaging: the tarball includes a small on-disk index and a tiny embedding server shim (no network calls required). That is the recommended path for the local run. See attached README inside the tarball (we included a seed index ~500 docs).

2) Model sizing: for candidate generation we recommend a small to medium open LLM (e.g., the 7B float/quantized variant) as a candidate. Rescoring can be performed on CPU if you use a simpler linear re-ranker, but for neural rescoring use a 2-4GB GPU card. For your environment: run candidate gen on the 8GB GPUs and rescoring on 16GB if you want margin. We'll provide a low-cost fallback variant to keep the loud traffic within budget.

3) Auth flow: for the initial POC, static API_KEY in auth-config-example.env is fastest. If you want a short TTL we can share a 5-line token exchange pattern (Auth server -> Redwood short-lived key) — I can paste that if you want to test a rotation.

Routing snippet (Python):
- import redwood_sdk
- client = redwood_sdk.Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
- response_candidates = client.generate(model='rw-7b-cand', input=prompt, top_k=20)
- rerank_scores = client.rerank(model='rw-ranker-small', candidates=response_candidates)
- final = select_best(rerank_scores)

I'll drop a minimal TypeScript example in the shared Drive by EOD. If you want it earlier, ping me and I'll post the gist.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Claire — quick confirmation from our side: the local-test-checklist.pdf has an explicit smoke test you can run that verifies the end-to-end path (auth -> candidate -> embed -> rerank -> structured output). Key things to confirm in your run:

- The sample completes under 90s on a single 8GB GPU for the candidate step.
- Reranking step produces a 5-10x narrower list and returns structured JSON with keys {answer, provenance, tool_call}.
- The tool_call placeholder demonstrates how to call an external tool (we used a mock URL in the sample).

If your Friday run completes, can you drop a short recording or logs into the Drive folder above and we'll review during the Monday sync? If anything blocks, we can stand up a short debug session (30m) on Sunday.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
